title: CLCON/49/2010 of SATYA BAHAR Vs SMT MANISHA PANWAR SECRETARY and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Contempt Application No. 49 of 2010
Satya Bahar S/o Shri Tirath Singh ..... Petitioner
Versus
Smt. Manisha Panwar, Secretary and others ..... Respondents
Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Brief Holder for respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3.
Mr. Parikshit Saini, Advocate for respondent Nos. 4 and 5.
Hon'ble Tarun Agarwala, J.
Heard Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, the learned counsel for the
applicant, Shri Subhash Upadhyay, the learned Brief Holder for the
respondent Nos. 1, 2 & 3 and Shri Parikshit Saini, the learned
counsel for respondent Nos. 4 and 5.
The present contempt application has been filed for alleged
willful disobedience of the order of the writ court dated 1st March,
2006 as affirmed by the order of the appellate court dated 15th
December, 2009 passed in Special Appeal.
The brief facts leading to the filing of the contempt
application is, that a short term vacancy arose in an educational
institution known as Raja Mahendra Pratap Prem Vidayalaya.
Pursuant to the said vacancy, selection process was initiated by the
Committee of Management and the applicant was appointed as an
Assistant Teacher on an adhoc basis. The papers were forwarded to
the District Inspector of School for necessary approval. No approval
was sent and, consequently, the applicant filed a writ petition before
the Allahabad High Court which was disposed of with the direction
to the authority to consider and decide the representation. It
transpires that the representation was not decided and the applicant
again filed another writ petition before this Court after the creation
of the Uttarakhand which was again disposed of with the necessary
direction to the authority. It transpires that the District Inspector of
School by an order dated 17th May, 2004 rejected the representation
of the applicant holding that the applicant was not entitled for

2
payment of any salary as his appointment was not made in
accordance with the procedure. The petitioner, being aggrieved,
filed a writ petition No. 454 of 2005 (S/S) before this Court which
was allowed by a judgment dated 1st March, 2006. The writ court
quashed the order dated 17th May, 2004 and directed the respondent
No.3, namely, the District Education Officer, Haridwar to pass
appropriate orders with regard to the payment of salary to the
petitioner admissible in L.T. grade w.e.f. 1st November, 1996.
Against this order, the respondents filed a special appeal
No. 151 of 2006 which was eventually dismissed by a judgment
dated 15th December, 2009. The appellate court observed :-
"We are satisfied that the appellants should pay costs
quantified at Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand). The
aforesaid costs shall be deposited by the appellants with the
High Court Bar Association of Uttarakhand. The receipt of
costs deposited shall be placed on the record of this case
within one month from today, failing which, the instant
Special Appeal shall be re-listed for motion hearing, for the
recovery of costs. The entire wages/salary payable to the
respondent Satya Bahar Shall be positively disbursed to him
within one month of the receipt of a certified copy of this
order."
The appellate court directed the respondents to pay the entire
wages payable to the applicant to be positively disbursed within one
month and also imposed costs at Rs.10,000/-.
Not being satisfied, the respondents preferred a Special Leave
Petition before the Supreme Court of India which was dismissed by
an order dated 19/04/2010.
When all doors stood closed, the Director of Education
eventually passed an order dated 19th May, 2010 directing the
authority to release the salary. Based on the said direction, the
Secretary issued a consequential order dated 1st June, 2010. It
transpires that the arrears of salary for the period 1st November, 1996
to 31st May, 2000 was eventually paid to the applicant.

3
In the meanwhile, since the order of the writ court as affirmed
by the appellate court and Supreme Court had not been complied
with, the applicant filed the present contempt application on 3rd May,
2010. Confused with the issuance of the contempt notice, the
authorities directed the Committee of Management to prepare the
salary bills for the period 1st June, 2000 to 6th December, 2007 and,
based on the direction of the Finance Officer, the Committee of
Management prepared the necessary bills and forwarded it to the
District Education Officer. It transpires that the Finance Officer
approved the bills and a sum of Rs.8,80,000/- for the period 1st June,
2000 to 30th November, 2007 was paid directly to the applicant.
Subsequently, it revealed that the applicant did not work in
the education institution for the period 1st June, 2000 to 6th
December, 2007 and the respondents found that the applicant was
not entitled for payment of salary. It has come on record that the
respondents instituted an Inquiry Committee, who in turn, has seized
the necessary records of the Committee of Management, namely, the
attendance register, salary register, etc. for the relevant period.
It has also come on record that the amount of Rs. 8.80 lacs
which was received by the applicant on 21.11.2011 was
subsequently refunded by the applicant on 10th March, 2012 and 12th
March, 2012. According to the applicant, the amount was returned
under duress being imposed by the respondents.
Be that as it may. The controversy according to the applicant
which now boils down is non-payment of arrears of salary for the
period 1st June, 2000 to 6th December, 2007.
It has come on record that the applicant had applied for leave
without pay for the period 7th December, 2007 to 31st March, 2010.
At the same time, it has come on record that the applicant has joined
as an Assistant Teacher in a Government Primary School Mundat
w.e.f. 6th January, 2009. Consequently, it can safely be presumed
that the applicant was no longer a teacher in Raja Mahendra Pratap
Prem Vidayalaya w.e.f. 6th January, 2009.

4
This Court by an order dated 14th March, 2012 had directed
the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 to be present before this Court and
produce the entire record during the period the applicant has alleged
to have worked in the institution concerned. Based on the aforesaid
direction, respondent Nos. 3 and 4 are present in court today
alongwith the record. The record has been perused by the learned
counsel for the applicant as well as by the learned counsel for
respondent Nos. 4 and 5. The learned counsel for respondent Nos. 4
and 5 has stated that the Manager and the Principal are also present
and has further stated that the original record produced by the
respondent No.3 is the same which was seized from them.
A perusal of the record indicates that the name of the
applicant is not entered in the attendance register nor is found in the
salary register for the period 01.06.2000 to 30.11.2007.
In the light of the aforesaid, the learned counsel for the
respondent No. 3 urged that the order of the writ court as affirmed by
the appellate court and the Supreme Court has been complied with in
letter and in spirit and that there is no willful violation of the order of
the writ court by any of the authorities. The applicant has been paid
his salary for the period he had worked and is not entitled to be paid
the salary w.e.f. 1st June, 2000 onwards since he had not worked in
the institution concerned. In this regard, the learned counsel for the
applicant submitted that no affidavit has been filed nor at any stage it
has been indicated that the applicant had never worked whereas the
applicant has categorically stated in paragraph 6 of the contempt
application that he has not been paid his salary from 1st November,
1996 onwards and that he is working w.e.f. 1st November, 1996
onwards.
Even though the applicant has stated that he is working w.e.f.
1st January, 1996 (wrongly mentioned as 1st January, 1996) whereas
it should be 1st November, 1996, the said statement based on
affidavit, cannot be taken into consideration, inasmuch as, paragraph
6 of the affidavit is based on legal advice and such legal advice
being given cannot be taken as the evidentiary value. This view of

5
mine is further fortified by the fact that the applicant had filed the
contempt application on 3rd May, 2010 and did not reveal the fact
that he had left the institution and had joined as an Assistant Teacher
in Govt. Primary School Mundat w.e.f. 6th January, 2009 which is a
serious concealment of material fact which the applicant did not
disclose. Consequently, the averments made in paragraph 6 of the
affidavit supporting the contempt application cannot be taken into
consideration.
The court of is of the opinion that in the light of subsequent
facts which has been brought on record coupled with the fact that the
original attendance register and salary register for the period 1st June,
2000 onwards has been placed before the perusal of the court from
which the Court opines that the applicant prima-facie had not
worked as an Assistant Teacher in the institution concerned w.e.f. 1st
June, 2000 onwards. On the principal of no work no pay, the
applicant is not entitled for any arrears of salary for a period 1st June,
2000 onwards.
For the reasons stated aforesaid, this Court is of the opinion
that substantial compliance of the order of the writ court as affirmed
upto the stage of the Supreme Court has been made by the opposite
parties. The applicant has been paid the salary upto 30th May, 2000.
Prima facie, the applicant is not entitled to be paid salary for the
period 1st June, 2000 onwards since the Court is of the opinion that
the applicant had not worked and consequently, was not entitled to
arrears of salary. Since substantial compliance of the order of the
writ court has now been made by the opposite parties, notices are
discharged and the contempt application is dismissed. The original
record produced shall be taken back by the authority concerned.
 (Tarun Agarwala, J.)
Dated 10th April, 2012 Shiv
